modelingNotes: Neighborhood Theatre, NoDa, Charlotte (1945 cinema, now a music venue) — procedural, CC0-1.0. bun generators/neighborhood-theatre.ts

Map frame: x east, y north, z up, metres, placed at bearing 52°: the model's +y runs back from East 36th Street along the outline's long side (way/967830177, 16.9 × 33.6 m), so the street front is the model's south face. The anchor is the outline's centroid.

A small club is its front: a stepped parapet, taller in the middle, painted with the big colourful mural; a three-sided marquee box over the doors (OSM draws its roof, way/1411146348: 6.3 m at the wall, 2 m at the front, 2.7 m deep); flat attraction boards on the wall either side; a plain stucco ground floor with the doors and poster cases. Behind it the auditorium is a plain box. The boards carry no lettering; they are the `entrance` material so the marquee lights up at night, as the real one does.
The street slopes away behind the theatre: lidar puts the front sidewalk 3.0 m above the lowest ground at the back, so the walls run down to y = 0 and the front starts at G.

Rework (2026-10): forms kept (stepped front, mural, three-sided marquee, side boards, plain auditorium). Changes, each from the Mecklenburg 2016 lidar (USGS 3DEP, 0.5 m cells, sampled in this frame) and the 2024 street photo:
G 2.0 -> 3.0 m: lidar ground 3.0 m at the front sidewalk, 0 at the rear.

The marquee was 1.1 m too high: lidar puts its top 3.8 m above the sidewalk, and the photo (scaled by the 7.7 m centre parapet) its board 2.6-3.7 m. The side boards and the mural's lower edge move down with it.
Parapets: centre 7.7 m above the sidewalk (was 9.6), sides 6.95 (was 8.2). Centre section 7.0 m wide (was 8.4), from lidar and the photo.

The auditorium roof is a shallow ridge running front to back, not flat: lidar reads 9.3 m at both side walls and 10.3 m on the centre line. The lidar sits about 1.4 m east of OSM here (the marquee centres differ by that); the outline and marquee plan stay on OSM.

Measured: outline and marquee plan (OSM), every height (lidar). Estimated: the boards, doors and poster cases, from the photo. The mural is reduced to a warm field with three teal sweeps; its real reds, yellows and pinks are averaged into the warm colour.

References: City Dweller 2, "Neighborhood Theatre Mid-April 2024", "... along 36th St" and "... alley" (Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0); James Willamor, "Neighborhood Theater, NoDa, Charlotte - panoramio" (Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0).

Original procedural model from https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks (catalog id "neighborhood-theatre", model "neighborhood-theatre"), generated by https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks/blob/c3921f733df14b41e1f6d15853cce7b343886f17/generators/neighborhood-theatre.ts. That repository is the editable source; source.blend.gz is the exported mesh imported into Blender for convenience.

Exported for Open Landmarks v1: placement bearing and scale baked in; moving parts frozen in their rest pose; footings and basements below the lowest ground (y = 0) cut away; material colours carried over exactly, as library finishes where they are not standard swatches.
Window panels clipped to the walls behind them; 1 m² of glazing with no wall behind it (curtain walls, glazing past a wall's edge) uses the neighborhood-theatre-glazing finish in the window colour.
To fit six materials, folded neighborhood-theatre-mural-teal into roof (ΔE 17.2).
